Who we are · Beta-i · Collaborative innovation collaborative innovation Home On the homepage What you can expect Our approach Track record Numbers Our work Beyond one organisation Coalitions What we do Three models What we do Work Cases by model Strategic direction Operating model Corporate venturing All of it Every case Searchable Who we are Careers Share your challenge Who we are The future is made together. A team of first movers, born in Lisbon in 2009 to set the pace of an innovation ecosystem that barely existed yet. More than fifteen years later we work from Lisbon, Brussels, Boston and Sao Paulo, and the habit has not changed: we go first, and we take people with us. Where the work happens “It is the first time that we are doing this, but it is not the first time that we are doing things for the first time .” Our CEO, more often than he probably realises It is the closest thing we have to a job description. Nobody calls us because the path is known. They call us because it is not, and because somebody has to go first and bring the others along. Fifteen years of first times have taught us something that cannot be read in a method: how to move when the map runs out, how to keep several organisations moving together while it happens, and how to tell the difference between a risk worth taking and a detour. The facts Client Jose de Mello Context A diversified group's holding company Year 2026 Service line Operating model Format AI strategy and readiness sprint, with practical enablement and prototyping Audience Board, executive committee, directors and holding teams Our role Leadership and team enablement, opportunity mapping, pilot selection, prototype development and governance design Download the one pager ↓ All cases in this model Working side by side with Jose de Mello's holding teams, we connected AI learning with real business challenges. AI Ignite combined leadership development, practical experimentation and governance foundations, helping teams turn opportunities into prototypes and build the capability to continue. The problem Jose de Mello wanted to translate AI's potential into a practical way of working for its holding teams, while preparing the holding to
The problem Jose de Mello wanted to translate AI's potential into a practical way of working for its holding teams, while preparing the holding to support adoption across the wider group.
How it runs 01 Build fluency across leadership and teams We delivered three executive sessions and three team sessions, supported by individual executive mentoring.
Leaders explored AI's strategic implications, governance and measurement, while teams learnt to identify use cases and create simple agents responsibly.
04 Create the foundations for continuity The work included a use case catalogue and good practice framework, an AI committee design and recommendations for ownership, human oversight and measurement.
What came out of it Jose de Mello gained a prioritised AI opportunity pipeline, three developed business prototypes and practical assistants configured with its teams.
Why it matters here AI adoption takes hold when people can connect it to their work and have the confidence, ownership and support to act.
It shows how AI Ignite builds organisational capability alongside the first solutions.
